# Touch Padel operator app — compact map

Generated by packages/db/scripts/build-assistant-map.mjs; do not edit. Roles in brackets; rail location after the route.

## Pages

- / [any signed-in staff (it only redirects)] — No screen of its own: it shows the boot screen until the staff row loads, then redirects to /workspaces when the account holds several workspaces and none is stored on this station, otherwise to the role's home (/till, /kds, /desk/today, /ops, /panel or /tasks).
- /admin [manager, owner] — A layout with no content of its own: it draws the section tab strip for the Menu and Guest-app families and its index redirects to /admin/menu.
- /admin/addons [manager, owner] — The "Add-ons" screen listing item groups and sub-groups of guest choices; "New group" and "New sub-group" open an editor that saves with app.upsert_modifier_group and app.link_item_modifier_group, options save through app.upsert_modifier, and reveals through app.set_modifier_reveals. For a manager an option on sale keeps its price, with "Change the price" (an addon_price price or promo change on /protocols), and a new paid option is saved hidden with its switch off and "Put on sale"; a free option is added and switched as before. A manager's save that would make guests pay more (a paid choice made compulsory by a group's minimum, a link, a reveal, or a free option switched off or moved) is refused and said to be the owner's to make.
- /admin/audit [manager, owner] (Operations: "Audit log"; Management › Observe: "Audit log") — The read-only "Audit log": who did what and why, with period, search, area and actor filters and a "missing reason" toggle; the buttons only refresh, clear filters, expand a row's before and after values, or export CSV.
- /admin/categories [manager, owner] — The "Categories" screen for the menu sections' order, photo, tax group and shown or hidden switch; "New category" or a row opens the form whose "Save" calls app.upsert_menu_category, and the order arrows call app.reorder_menu_categories.
- /admin/courts [manager, owner] (Management › Setup: "Courts") — The "Courts" admin listing bookable courts in calendar order; "Add court" and "Edit" open a panel with names, photo, indoor or outdoor, booking lengths and an open switch saved by app.upsert_court, with "Switch off" (app.delete_court) and order arrows (app.reorder_courts).
- /admin/day-close [manager, owner] (Operations: "Day close"; Management › Financial: "Day close") — The day-close screen: when no trading day is open it shows an opening-float field and "Open day" (app.open_day); otherwise it walks the steps (settle open tabs, wait for tills to sync, count the cash, enter the card batch) and "Close day" calls app.close_day, with "Export CSV" for the day's figures; unpaid played bookings and "Checklists not finished" (the daily lists with a line nobody ticked, from app.checklist_day_state) warn but do not block.
- /admin/hero [manager, owner] (Management › Setup: "Guest site") — The "Guest site home screen" builder choosing what sits above the guest menu ("Menu only", "Photo or video" or "Featured item"), the ticker lines and the bell tutorial switch; "Save" writes the cafe settings in one call (app.set_cafe_settings) and "Discard changes" reverts. For a manager the featured discount is read-only with "Change the discount" (a featured_discount price or promo change on /protocols) and, while one is stored, "Switch the discount off" (saves 0); while a discount is stored the featured item picker is off, and so is the Featured tile when the hero is not already in Featured mode.
- /admin/hours [manager, owner] — The "Opening hours" page setting each day's open and close times and the closed dates; "Save" calls app.set_opening_hours, and the same editor is the first tab of /admin/settings.
- /admin/menu [manager, owner] (Operations: "Menu"; Management › Financial: "Menu prices") — The "Menu items" editor listing categories and their items with sold-out switches; "New category" and "New item" open forms that save through app.upsert_menu_category and app.upsert_menu_item, the arrows reorder with app.reorder_menu_items, and the switch calls app.set_item_sold_out. For a manager, "New item" in a café category is "Propose a new item", which opens a product release on /protocols; a launched item's sizes show their prices read-only with "Change the price" (a price change on /protocols) instead of "New size"; a never-launched café item's Active switch is off with "Goes on sale when the owner launches it", and a hidden shop product that was never on sale shows "Put on sale" (a shop_launch change). An item still in its product release is marked "In release" and its form names the release with "Open the release"; nobody can switch it on or change its prices here.
- /admin/promotions [manager, owner] (Operations: "Promotions"; Management › Observe: "Promotions" (not a printed rail row)) — The "Promotions" list with a lifecycle filter, a search box and a per-row on/off switch (app.set_promotion_enabled); "New promotion" or a row opens the promotion editor whose "Save" calls app.upsert_promotion, and nothing is ever deleted. Only the owner saves a promotion or generates its code; a manager may switch a promotion off, and otherwise gets "Propose a promotion", "Change this promotion" in the read-only editor and "Switch on" beside a switched-off one, each a price or promo change on /protocols.
- /admin/qr [manager, owner] (Management › Setup: "Tables & QR") — The "Tables & QR" screen listing cafe tables with zone, seats and a waiter-bell switch (app.set_table_bell); "Add table" and a row edit a table (app.upsert_cafe_table), "Print all cards" and "Print this card" print A6 QR cards, and "Replace" or "Replace every QR code" rotate tokens with app.rotate_table_token.
- /admin/rates [manager, owner] (Operations: "Rates"; Management › Financial: "Rates") — The "Court rates" screen listing rate rules by court, days, time window, prices and priority; "New rule" or a row opens the editor whose "Save" calls app.upsert_rate_rule and affects only new bookings, and a toggle shows or hides switched-off rules. Only the owner saves a rule; a manager reads them, with "Propose a new rate" and, on an open rule, "Change this rate", each a rate price or promo change on /protocols.
- /admin/settings [manager, owner] (Management › Setup: "Venue settings") — "Venue settings" in four tabs: Opening hours (app.set_opening_hours), Day & service (business-day start hour, waiter-call wait via app.set_waiter_call_cooldown, idle lock), Analytics (owner-only exclusions and engagement floor) and Venue details (name, phone, timezone through app.set_venue_details).
- /admin/staff [owner] (Management › Setup: "Staff") — The owner's "Staff" screen listing accounts with role, PIN and status; "Add staff member" creates an account through the staff-admin edge function; opened from a hiring run's add_staff step (?hire=) a banner names the picked candidate and the role (app.protocol_step_detail, app.protocol_run_detail, app.hiring_candidates), "Add the new staff member" opens the form filled in with the role fixed, and the new account is sent as the step through app.submit_step, which finishes the run; "Manage" opens an editor (app.rename_staff, set_staff_role, set_staff_active, set_staff_pin, clear_staff_pin, set_station_staff for cover), and the breaks panel's "Save" writes break_allowance_minutes. Kitchen (prep) is retired: it is not offered for a new account or a role change (kitchen staff are Head barista, Barista, Head chef or Chef), and an account still on it shows a "Retired" badge and keeps working until it is moved.
- /admin/suggested [manager, owner] — The "Suggested items" screen picking the "Goes well with" list shown under an item on the guest menu; add or "Remove" suggestions up to the cap, then "Save" (or "Discard changes") writes app.set_addon_suggestions.
- /admin/telegram [owner] (Management › Observe: "Telegram" (not a printed rail row)) — The "Telegram" settings with "Set up" and "Sent messages" tabs: connection health from the telegram-diagnose function, "Send test message" (app.telegram_send_test), the group chat id and message language saved as cafe settings, and the people who may press the bot's buttons set with app.set_telegram_staff.
- /analytics [owner] (Management: "Analytics") — A layout that validates the shared search params (range, custom dates, compare basis, court) and redirects to /analytics/courts, carrying the search along; the Courts and Cafe tabs switch between the two analytics screens.
- /analytics/cafe [owner] — Owner-only Cafe analytics: Summary, What stands out, Menu, Sales and the guest menu, and Busy times, fed by app.analytics_daily_sales, _sold_items, _best_sellers, _bought_together, _item_margins, _price_bands, _promo, _menu_snapshot and _hourly plus PostHog guest data; the bar carries period, compare and the "Business day" and "Excluded items" settings, "Export" saves the figures, and the AI card's "Ask for findings" and "Check they still hold" call the insights function and save its results.
- /analytics/courts [owner] — Owner-only Courts analytics: Summary, What stands out, When courts are busy, Courts compared, Cancellations and no-shows, How people book, Guests, and Court players at the cafe, fed by app.analytics_courts_summary, _demand, _endings, _guests and _cafe for the period and its comparison window; the Summary names "Event hours" (courts held for tournaments, counted as open hours) when there were any; the bar sets range, compare basis and court, "Export" saves the figures, and tiles drill into transactions.
- /assistant [owner] (Management: "Assistant") — The owner assistant: a full page with the list of chats, the thread, the context checkboxes with their pack sizes, and the usage meter; "Ask" sends a question (billed), "Stop" ends a streaming answer, "Run this job" accepts an estimate, and every answer lists the tools it read with a link to the page that shows the same numbers.
- /assistant/usage [owner] — What the assistant has cost: tokens by kind (input, cache write, cache read, output) and cost per day for the month, month-to-date against the cap, and the price table each model is billed from.
- /desk [court_desk, manager, owner] (Court desk: "Calendar"; Operations: "Bookings"; Management › Observe: "Bookings" (not a printed rail row)) — The desk calendar: a courts × half-hour grid for one day or a month heat view, where pressing a free slot opens the booking dialog (reservation.create → app.staff_create_reservation) and dragging a booking moves it (reservation.update → app.move_reservation); "New series" and "Block court" lead to their own screens.
- /desk/block [court_desk, manager, owner] (Court desk: "Block court") — The "Block court" form (court, date, from, to, reason); its "Block court" button creates a maintenance reservation (reservation.create), shows a conflict notice when the window is already taken, then offers "Open calendar" and "Block another". Opened from a tournament's courts step (?run=&step=) it is "Block courts for a tournament" instead: the plan's courts and times from app.tournament_context, each "Blocked" or "To block"; "Block N remaining" calls app.block_courts_for_event, which blocks them all as the tournament's event or, with a booking in the way, blocks nothing and lists what to move ("Open booking", "Check again"); then "Send courts step" submits the step with the blocks of the plan's windows and an optional note (app.submit_step). A plan sent back and moved has already given its old blocks back.
- /desk/customers [court_desk, cashier, manager, owner] (Court desk: "Customers"; Till: "Customers") — Customer search that queries app.customer_search as you type; each result offers "Book" and "Open", "Create customer" goes to the new-customer form, and in attach mode "Attach to booking" or "Attach to tab" hands the chosen customer back to the caller.
- /desk/customers/new [court_desk, manager, owner] — The "New customer" form (full name, phone, optional email, preferred language); "Create customer" calls the staff-gated desk-customer-create edge function, which creates a real guest account, and opens the new record, while "Cancel" returns to search.
- /desk/series/new [court_desk, manager, owner] (Court desk: "New series") — The "New series" screen for a repeating booking; "Check clashes" previews every date with app.preview_series, each clash is resolved with "Skip this date" or "Move to another court", and "Create series" writes the plan through app.create_series.
- /desk/today [court_desk, manager, owner] (Court desk: "Today") — The "Today" board of arrivals, courts in play now and every booking today; "Mark arrived" writes app.mark_reservation, "New booking" and "Book this court" open the create-booking dialog, "Find customer" goes to /desk/customers, and "Take payment" opens the booking's bill.
- /financial [owner] (Management › Financial: "Overview") — The Financial section's landing screen: a "This month so far" card from app.panel_headline (earned, cash, card) beside "Cash at recent day closes" read from day_sessions; "Open the management panel" goes to /panel, "Go to day close" to /admin/day-close, and the cards below open the section's screens.
- /kds [prep, head_barista, barista, head_chef, chef, manager, owner] — The kitchen display board: its live tickets, and those completed in the last two minutes, are read through app.kitchen_board with their lines, add-ons, notes and ready marks and no prices; per-ticket "Start", "Ready" and "Complete" buttons move the ticket through its statuses (ticket.status → app.set_ticket_status), ticking one item calls app.set_order_item_ready, and "Leave kitchen display" appears only for staff who hold another workspace.
- /marketing [owner] (Management › Observe: "Marketing") — The owner's campaign list from app.marketing_overview showing status, window, audience and what each campaign brought in (or "Not measurable"); drafts the marketing role suggested (app.marketing_suggestions) are marked with who sent them, their note and photos, with a "From marketing" filter; a read-only "Requests to marketing" panel (app.marketing_requests_page) lists what staff asked marketing for from their phones, Waiting, Answered or All, with who asked, the item, the date wanted, the photos and marketing's answer; "New campaign" and "Edit campaign" save through app.save_marketing_campaign, per-row "Schedule", "Set live" and "End" confirm then call app.set_campaign_status, "New audience" writes app.save_marketing_audience, and "Open promotions" and "Open Telegram" link out.
- /observation [owner] (Management › Observe: "Overview") — The Observe section's landing screen: a "Waiting on you" list built from app.staff_requests_page and app.marketing_overview with "Answer requests" and "Review campaigns", the Live floor 3D plan, and screen cards fed by app.ops_overview.
- /observation/courts [owner] (Management › Observe: "Bookings") — A view-only "Bookings" board for a chosen day or month: a figure strip, one card per court right now, the night in two-hour rows and a month heat calendar, all read from reservations; "Refresh" re-reads, and pressing a booking opens a read-only panel whose only button is "Open in Court desk".
- /observation/requests [owner] (Management › Observe: "Requests") — The owner's decision queue for leave, shift swaps, wage advances and record corrections from app.staff_requests_page, filtered by Awaiting decision, Decided or All; "Approve" and "Decline" open a dialog that calls app.decide_staff_request (a decline needs a reason), and a decision is final.
- /observation/tills [owner] (Management › Observe: "Tills") — A view-only "Tills" board of the cafe floor for one business day: running, settled, voided and waiter-call figures, occupied and free tables, and lists of open, settled and void tabs read from tabs; "Refresh" re-reads, and a tab opens a read-only panel whose only button is "Open in Cashier".
- /ops [manager, owner] (Operations: "Today"; Management › Observe: "Floor now") — The manager's "Today" screen, refreshed from app.ops_overview every 30 seconds: a "Needs you now" list with "Open the day", "Answer calls", "See which" and "Review expired"; courts, cafe and stock cards with "Open bookings", "Open tabs" and "Open stock"; the day-close steps ending in "Go to day close"; exceptions, staff activity, and "Refresh".
- /panel [owner] (Management: "Management panel") — The owner's read-only landing screen: app.panel_headline fills an "Earned" and "Taken in payments" band plus padel, cafe and losses figure rows for a chosen range and comparison, each figure opening its transactions through app.report_drill; "Export CSV" writes the window, every figure and every drill transaction to one file, and buttons open the Courts, Cafe, Revenue, Stock and Staff reports.
- /protocols [manager, owner] — Protocols: cards for New item, Tournament, Hiring, Price or promo change and Daily checklists, each showing how many are running and waiting on you with a Start button; Waiting on you, In progress and Finished lists from app.protocol_runs_page; a run opens its steps, records, photos and decisions (app.protocol_run_detail), a step's form submits through app.submit_step, Approve, Send back, Stop and Skip call app.decide_step or app.skip_step (a reason is required for the last three), Launch goes through the protocol-action function, and the owner-only How it works sheet saves app.save_protocol_template; the Daily checklists card (app.checklist_day_state) opens today's lists with who ticked each line and the photo of a line that needs one (app.checklist_board), and the owner's list editor, where any line can be switched to "Needs a photo", saves app.save_checklist_template.
- /reports [manager, owner] — A layout with no content of its own that redirects to /reports/courts; the tab strip (Revenue, Courts, Cafe, Stock, Staff activity) shows the reports the current role and Management section may open.
- /reports/cafe [manager, owner] — The cafe report (app.report_cafe, or app.report_compare): revenue, orders, average order, items sold, gross profit and margin and prep time with the "Show" views Best sellers, Cost & profit, By category and Waste, a "See waste" button that lists every write-off in the period, "Export", and item rows that drill their sold lines through app.report_drill.
- /reports/courts [manager, owner] (Operations: "Reports") — The courts report (app.report_courts, or app.report_compare): totals for bookings, booked hours, occupancy, court revenue, cancellations and no-shows, plus "Event hours" (courts held for tournaments, counted as open hours) as a figure and a By court column when a tournament held a court, with the "Show" views By court, Cancellations, Peak times, By start time and By day, a court filter and "Export"; a court or day row drills its bookings through app.report_drill.
- /reports/revenue [owner] (Management › Financial: "Reports") — The owner-only revenue report (app.report_revenue, or app.report_compare when a comparison is chosen): headline figures grouped as Earned, Money taken, Given away and Tax, a day, week or month breakdown with the "Show" views Earned, Money taken, Given away and Tax, staff and payment-method filters, "Export", and pressing a figure or row opens its transactions through app.report_drill.
- /reports/staff [manager, owner] (Management › Observe: "Staff activity") — The staff activity report (app.report_staff_activity): one row per person with the "Show" views Activity, "Discounts, voids & refunds", Waiter calls and Day closes, a staff filter and "Export"; each row's "Audit" opens /admin/audit for that person, and rows drill their transactions through app.report_drill.
- /reports/stock [manager, owner] (Management › Stock: "Stock value") — The stock value report (app.report_stock): headline stock value plus counts for running low, below par, expiring soon and expired, with the "Show" views Running low, Below par, Expiring soon, Expired, Used and Count differences (with an "Only differences" toggle and a Product tests column); each list has a button opening the matching /stock screen, plus "Export".
- /setup [owner] (Management › Setup: "Overview") — The Setup section's landing screen: a "Worth checking" panel flags a broken Telegram link, managers or owners without a PIN, a single owner account, active accounts still on the retired Kitchen role (update every station first, then move each one to Barista or Chef), and prepared items with no par level (the kitchen's "What to make today" never asks for them), each with a jump button ("Open Telegram", "Set PINs", "Go to Staff", "Open Ingredients"), above cards opening the Setup screens.
- /stock [manager, owner] (Operations: "Stock"; Management › Stock: "Inventory") — "On hand", the stock landing screen: a "Needs attention" list (running low, expired, sold past records, below par, expiring soon, open alerts) whose buttons are "Show which", "Open expiry" and "Open alerts", a searchable on-hand table from v_ingredient_on_hand and app.report_stock, header buttons "Record a delivery", "Record waste" and "Count stock" (or "Continue the count"), and a per-row "History" ledger drawer.
- /stock/alerts [manager, owner] — Stock alerts from manager_alerts grouped by kind (sold past what was on record, expired, running low, expiring soon, offline sale not applied), each group with "Dismiss all" and each row with "Dismiss" (app.acknowledge_alert) and a jump such as "Count stock", "Open expiry" or "See what is low".
- /stock/counts [manager, owner] — "Stock count": "Start count" opens a count (app.start_count), a blind-entry table follows (drafts saved locally, with a "Show recorded amounts" toggle), and "Finish count" confirms and calls app.finalize_count, then opens Count differences.
- /stock/expiry [manager, owner] — Expiry, from app.report_stock: an "Expired: throw out and write off" panel and an "Expiring soon: use first" panel listing batches with quantity left, worth and date; "Write off" opens a manager-PIN and reason dialog that calls app.write_off_expired, and the header has "Export".
- /stock/ingredients [manager, owner] — Ingredient master data (unit, supplier, pack size and price, shelf life, par, reorder point, yield, expected waste) from the ingredients table; "New ingredient" and per-row "Edit" open a dialog whose "Save" writes app.upsert_ingredient, and on-hand is a read-only figure linking to "Count stock".
- /stock/margins [manager, owner] — Margins per menu item from v_item_margin: an "Items that earn too little" panel with "Show which" for "Sell at a loss" and "Margin under 30%", over a searchable Price, Cost to make, Margin and Margin % table; read-only, and the empty state links to Recipes.
- /stock/products [manager, owner] — "Shop products": one row per size of every Touch Shop product (a menu item in a shop section) with SKU, barcode, price, on hand and supplier; "New product" writes app.upsert_menu_item then app.upsert_retail_variant, "Add size" and "Edit" write app.upsert_retail_variant, which keeps each size's own stock row (unit pc) in step. For a manager a product's prices go to the owner: a new product is saved hidden, a hidden product never on sale keeps its prices editable and offers "Put on sale" (a shop_launch price or promo change on /protocols), and a product on sale has its prices read-only with "Change the price" in place of "Add size", while its SKU, barcode, supplier, pack cost and low-stock level stay editable.
- /stock/receive [manager, owner] — "Goods in": "Bought by the driver" lists the driver's purchases still to receive (app.purchases_to_receive), and "Receive" opens one (?purchase=) prefilled with what was bought, where "Receive into stock" books its stock lines as one delivery through app.receive_purchase and "Mark checked" closes a line that is not stock (app.acknowledge_purchase_line); each purchase says "Delivered <time> by <name>" once the driver confirmed it reached the venue on the phone, or "Delivery not confirmed yet", and receiving never waits for it; below it, one delivery per submit with supplier and notes and per-line ingredient, received and ordered quantities, cost per unit and batch expiry; "Add another ingredient" adds a line and "Record delivery" posts the whole delivery through app.receive_delivery.
- /stock/recipes [manager, owner] — Recipes tabbed by Menu items, Add-ons and Prepared items with an All or No-recipe filter; "Add" or "Edit" opens a dialog where "Add an ingredient" adds lines and "Save" replaces the whole recipe atomically through app.set_recipe.
- /stock/suppliers [manager, owner] — "Suppliers": who the venue buys from (name, phone, notes, in use), picked on goods in and on shop products; "New supplier" and "Edit" write app.upsert_supplier, which refuses a second live supplier with the same spelling.
- /stock/variance [manager, owner] — "Count differences" for a chosen finished count from v_variance_report, defaulting to "Only differences" with a toggle to "All ingredients", with columns Records said, Counted, Difference, Sold, Expected waste, Recorded waste, Voids, Expired and Product tests (what a new item's test servings used, the product_test movements of a product release); each row has "History", where a product test's note opens its release on /protocols, and the header has "Export".
- /stock/waste [manager, owner] — "Waste & production", two forms side by side: "Record waste" (ingredient, quantity, Spill or Spoilage, a required note) writes app.record_waste, and "Record production" (prepared item, amount made) writes app.record_production, which consumes the components by recipe and reports the batch cost; below them "Made today" lists the business day's batches, from here or the kitchen's phones, with who made them (app.production_log_today).
- /tasks [driver, marketing] (Team: "My tasks") — "My tasks", the driver's and marketing's landing screen and the team workspace's one rail row; nothing can be assigned yet, so it shows only the empty state saying what will appear here once assigned (purchases and checklists for a driver, marketing tasks and checklists for marketing), with no buttons and no data read.
- /till [cashier, manager, owner] (Till: "Till") — The cashier's till: a search box, category strip and item grid feed a basket whose "Send to kitchen" posts the order (order.add_items → app.till_add_items), the active tab panel's "Cash" and "Card" buttons open the payment pane (tab.settle → app.settle_tab), and "New tab" (F6) opens a tab.
- /till/drawer [cashier, manager, owner] (Till: "Cash drawer"; Management › Financial: "Cash drawer") — The "Cash drawer" screen showing the opening float and today's drawer activity; "Open drawer" asks for a reason code and records the opening with app.record_drawer_open, and managers also see "Go to day close".
- /till/tabs [cashier, manager, owner] (Till: "Open tabs"; Operations: "Open tabs"; Management › Observe: "Tills" (not a printed rail row)) — The "Open tabs" board listing every tab on the floor with its age and running total; "Open tab" starts a new one, a row's "Open" jumps to the till with that tab selected, "Merge" combines two tabs (app.merge_tabs), and "Remove" cancels an empty tab (app.cancel_tab).
- /workspaces [manager, owner] — The "Choose a workspace" switcher, shown when an account holds more than one role; each workspace tile is a button that makes that workspace active and opens its home, with a "You are here" badge on the current one.

## Rules

### A discount, void, refund or price override needs a manager PIN and a reason
The money-adjustment RPCs (`apply_discount`, `override_price`, `void_after_send`, `refund`) take a PIN and a reason code, verify the PIN with `app.verify_manager_pin` (manager or owner PINs only, migration 0015), and record who applied and who authorised in the row and in the audit log. An invalid PIN is returned rather than raised so the five-failure lockout can engage (migration 0011); since 0105 every role may hold a PIN, but a cashier's PIN still cannot approve money.

### Breaks are counted per business day; cover is recorded, not signed in
A break (migration 0105) starts and ends with the person's own PIN, counts against `cafe_settings.break_allowance_minutes` (default 60) per business day, and is never cut short — a break that runs over is recorded with the overrun. While they are away another person assigned to the station in `station_staff` (or any manager or owner) can cover by entering their PIN; the machine's session stays the first person's, and the cover is written on the `staff_breaks` row and in the audit log, not minted as a login.

### Cash rounding is off
`venue_settings.cash_rounding_iqd` defaults to 1, which means no rounding (migration 0006, resolved override #1): a cash bill is charged exactly and `change_iqd` is exactly tendered minus amount. The knob exists for the venue to turn on later; today no figure has been rounded to 250 IQD.

### Comparison bases
The panel and `report_compare` (migrations 0068, 0103) compare with `previousPeriod` (the same number of days immediately before the range) or `sameLastYear` (the same dates one year earlier); the analytics pages use `prev` (the period before), `4w` (four weeks earlier) and `52w` (a year earlier) from `packages/core/src/analytics/range.ts`. Change is current minus previous, and a percentage change is shown only when the previous value is above zero; a key that is itself a percentage changes in points.

### Day close: open tabs and unsynced tills block it, unpaid bookings warn
`app.close_day` (migration 0020) refuses while any tab is open (DAY_OPEN_TABS) or any till still reports a non-empty replay queue (DAY_UNSYNCED); expected cash is the opening float plus cash payments minus cash refunds, and the variance against the counted drawer is stamped on the `day_sessions` row and never recomputed. Since migration 0106 the desk's cash and card are summed into the same close, and bookings played but not paid warn through `app.unpaid_played_bookings` without blocking.

### Every write leaves an audit row
Every mutating RPC calls `app.write_audit` (migration 0005) with an action string such as `tab.settle`, `reservation.move`, `order_item.void` or `staff.pin_set`, the entity, the actor, the reason code where one was required, and before/after values; /admin/audit reads it and the assistant's `audit_page` tool reads it with before/after reduced to the changed keys. A row without a reason on an action that required one is a finding, not a formatting quirk.

### Evidence floors for analytics claims
A figure is stated only when it rests on enough evidence (`packages/core/src/analytics/insightsContract.ts`): a rate is shown as a percentage only on at least 20 booked slots (otherwise "n of N"), a heat-map cell needs 4 open days, guest mix needs 15 identities, a cafe attach rate needs 10 live bookings, an ending cluster (cancellations, no-shows) needs 8 endings, and a cafe item claim needs 5 units sold or 5 views. Below the floor the assistant says the evidence is thin instead of quoting the number.

### Money is integer IQD
Every money column is a `bigint` through the domains `iqd` (never negative) and `iqd_signed` (deltas and variances) from migration 0002; there are no decimals, no floats and no fractional dinars on a bill, a report line or a day close. The one exception is the internal `unit_cost_iqd numeric(14,4)` on stock (cost per gram), which is rounded to whole dinars the moment it reaches a figure (design-data.md §2).

### Numbers in an answer come from a tool this turn
The assistant states a figure only when a tool returned it in the current turn, cites the tool, and prefers the aggregate RPC the page itself renders (`panel_headline`, `report_*`, `analytics_*`) over adding up rows, so its number and the page's number share the same business-day and basis rules (plan §7.2). A figure it cannot source is left out, and a figure under an evidence floor is described, not quoted.

### One live tab per booking; the court fee on a tab is what is still owed
Since migration 0106 a booking can have only one open or awaiting-payment tab (BOOKING_TAB_OPEN), and the court fee that tab carries is `app.court_fee_remaining`, the part of the booking price not yet paid, so a move or extension after payment charges only the difference and a cancelled or no-show booking charges nothing. `settle_tab` takes the total the clerk saw and raises TOTAL_CHANGED if the bill moved underneath them; a tab that owes nothing is closed with `app.settle_zero_tab`.

### Owner only
Only the owner role may open the assistant or call `app.assistant_run_tool`; managers, cashiers, prep and desk staff are refused with FORBIDDEN (contract decision 5, migration 0109). Answers therefore may include everything the owner can see in the app, and nothing the owner cannot.

### Payments, refunds, audit rows, stock movements and replays are append-only
`payments`, `refunds`, `audit_log`, `stock_movements` and `sync_replays` can only be inserted into, never updated or deleted, enforced twice: clients hold no UPDATE or DELETE grant, and a trigger (`app.forbid_mutation`, migration 0003, attached in 0005, 0015, 0018 and 0021) refuses the statement even for table owners (design-data.md §3.4). A wrong payment is corrected by a refund row, a wrong stock figure by a count adjustment movement, never by editing history.

### Prices are snapshotted by the server
Every order line's price is copied from the menu tables at the moment the order is created, by `app.create_guest_order` and `app.till_add_items` (migration 0015); clients never send a price. A later menu edit changes future orders only, and a rate rule saved on /admin/rates affects only new bookings.

### Promotions and campaigns are never deleted
Promotions (migration 0067) are switched off, never deleted, and their redemptions are replaced rather than edited; a marketing campaign (migration 0073) moves through its statuses only through `app.set_campaign_status`, and its result is the promotion's redemptions inside the campaign window — a campaign without a promotion is "Not measurable".

### Revenue is padel plus cafe net of refunds
Since migration 0099 one number is revenue everywhere: padel revenue (`reservations.price_iqd` of bookings in status confirmed, arrived or completed) plus cafe net (settled tabs' `total_iqd - court_iqd`, minus refunds). "Cafe revenue" on its own stays gross of refunds, and average order value divides the gross cafe by orders. A tab charged to a booking carries the court on its total (migration 0053), so the court is never counted twice.

### Roles come from the staff row, not the token
A person's role is whatever their active `staff` row says at the moment of the call: `app.staff_role()` and `app.is_staff(...)` (migration 0003) look the row up on every statement, never a JWT claim, so a role change by the owner takes effect on the next request without a new sign-in, and a deactivated account loses every screen at once. Guests hold the same `authenticated` role as staff, which is why every RPC guards itself on its first line.

### Sales basis: settled is money, served is activity
Item-level analytics take a basis (migration 0034): `settled` counts lines of tabs in status settled and reconciles with payments (the default the pages use); `served` also counts served orders on tabs not yet paid, for "today so far". Voided lines and voided orders are never counted on either basis, and `analytics_excluded_item_ids` is applied to item rankings only, never to money totals — revenue is revenue.

### Staff requests are decided once
A staff request (leave, shift swap, wage advance, record correction; migration 0072) is immutable once submitted apart from the owner's decision block; staff withdraw rather than edit, and an approve or decline on /observation/requests is final (a decline needs a reason).

### Stock: the movements ledger is the truth, batches are the index
`stock_movements` (migration 0018) is the only record of what came in and went out; `stock_batches` is a FEFO index (first expiry, first out) consumed by `app.consume_fefo` when orders are sent, and on-hand figures are sums of movements. A count (`finalize_count`, migration 0019) writes adjustment movements for the differences rather than overwriting a quantity, and an expired batch is written off through a PIN-gated RPC.

### The assistant is read-only
The assistant can read and explain but never change anything: every tool it calls goes through `app.assistant_run_tool` (migration 0109), a STABLE function that runs inside a read-only transaction under the owner's own session, dispatches only the fixed catalog of read RPCs, and has no branch that writes (plan §2.2, §7.1). When the owner asks for a change, the assistant says which page and which button does it and stops there.

### The business day starts at 04:00, not midnight
A row belongs to the business day given by `app.business_date(at)` (migration 0034): the venue's local wall clock shifted back by `cafe_settings.analytics_business_day_start_hour` (default 4, owner-editable on /admin/settings → Day & service), so a 01:30 sale belongs to the previous evening. Every report, analytics figure, break allowance and the panel bucket by this function; nothing reimplements it.

### The desk takes court payment into its own cash box
Court-desk staff may open, settle, merge and cancel tabs and record drawer openings (migration 0106) but cannot read `payments`, `refunds` or `tab_adjustments`; the desk gets its money figures from `app.booking_bill` and `app.booking_bill_states`, so no screen does money arithmetic. Refunds stay with managers and owners behind a PIN.

### Which timestamp puts a row in a day
Reports and the panel (migration 0068) bucket each source by one timestamp: reservations by `start_at` (whatever the status), settled tabs by `settled_at`, orders by `placed_at`, payments and refunds by their own `created_at`, adjustments by `created_at`, voids by the audit row's time, waste by the stock movement's time, and day closes by `closed_at`. A booking made today for next week counts next week.

chunks.title: /protocols
chunks.body:
Protocols: cards for New item, Tournament, Hiring, Price or promo change and Daily checklists, each showing how many are running and waiting on you with a Start button; Waiting on you, In progress and Finished lists from app.protocol_runs_page; a run opens its steps, records, photos and decisions (app.protocol_run_detail), a step's form submits through app.submit_step, Approve, Send back, Stop and Skip call app.decide_step or app.skip_step (a reason is required for the last three), Launch goes through the protocol-action function, and the owner-only How it works sheet saves app.save_protocol_template; the Daily checklists card (app.checklist_day_state) opens today's lists with who ticked each line and the photo of a line that needs one (app.checklist_board), and the owner's list editor, where any line can be switched to "Needs a photo", saves app.save_checklist_template.
Roles: manager, owner.
Not a rail row: reached from inside another screen or by URL.

chunks.title: /reports
chunks.body:
A layout with no content of its own that redirects to /reports/courts; the tab strip (Revenue, Courts, Cafe, Stock, Staff activity) shows the reports the current role and Management section may open.
Roles: manager, owner.
Not a rail row: reached from inside another screen or by URL.

chunks.title: /reports/cafe
chunks.body:
The cafe report (app.report_cafe, or app.report_compare): revenue, orders, average order, items sold, gross profit and margin and prep time with the "Show" views Best sellers, Cost & profit, By category and Waste, a "See waste" button that lists every write-off in the period, "Export", and item rows that drill their sold lines through app.report_drill.
Roles: manager, owner.
Not a rail row: reached from inside another screen or by URL.

chunks.title: /reports/courts — Reports
chunks.body:
The courts report (app.report_courts, or app.report_compare): totals for bookings, booked hours, occupancy, court revenue, cancellations and no-shows, plus "Event hours" (courts held for tournaments, counted as open hours) as a figure and a By court column when a tournament held a court, with the "Show" views By court, Cancellations, Peak times, By start time and By day, a court filter and "Export"; a court or day row drills its bookings through app.report_drill.
Roles: manager, owner.
Reached from: Operations: "Reports".

chunks.title: /reports/revenue — Reports
chunks.body:
The owner-only revenue report (app.report_revenue, or app.report_compare when a comparison is chosen): headline figures grouped as Earned, Money taken, Given away and Tax, a day, week or month breakdown with the "Show" views Earned, Money taken, Given away and Tax, staff and payment-method filters, "Export", and pressing a figure or row opens its transactions through app.report_drill.
Roles: owner.
Reached from: Management › Financial: "Reports".

chunks.title: /reports/staff — Staff activity
chunks.body:
The staff activity report (app.report_staff_activity): one row per person with the "Show" views Activity, "Discounts, voids & refunds", Waiter calls and Day closes, a staff filter and "Export"; each row's "Audit" opens /admin/audit for that person, and rows drill their transactions through app.report_drill.
Roles: manager, owner.
Reached from: Management › Observe: "Staff activity".

chunks.title: /reports/stock — Stock value
chunks.body:
The stock value report (app.report_stock): headline stock value plus counts for running low, below par, expiring soon and expired, with the "Show" views Running low, Below par, Expiring soon, Expired, Used and Count differences (with an "Only differences" toggle and a Product tests column); each list has a button opening the matching /stock screen, plus "Export".
Roles: manager, owner.
Reached from: Management › Stock: "Stock value".

chunks.title: /setup — Overview
chunks.body:
The Setup section's landing screen: a "Worth checking" panel flags a broken Telegram link, managers or owners without a PIN, a single owner account, active accounts still on the retired Kitchen role (update every station first, then move each one to Barista or Chef), and prepared items with no par level (the kitchen's "What to make today" never asks for them), each with a jump button ("Open Telegram", "Set PINs", "Go to Staff", "Open Ingredients"), above cards opening the Setup screens.
Roles: owner.
Reached from: Management › Setup: "Overview".

chunks.title: /stock — Stock / Inventory
chunks.body:
"On hand", the stock landing screen: a "Needs attention" list (running low, expired, sold past records, below par, expiring soon, open alerts) whose buttons are "Show which", "Open expiry" and "Open alerts", a searchable on-hand table from v_ingredient_on_hand and app.report_stock, header buttons "Record a delivery", "Record waste" and "Count stock" (or "Continue the count"), and a per-row "History" ledger drawer.
Roles: manager, owner.
Reached from: Operations: "Stock"; Management › Stock: "Inventory".

chunks.title: /stock/alerts
chunks.body:
Stock alerts from manager_alerts grouped by kind (sold past what was on record, expired, running low, expiring soon, offline sale not applied), each group with "Dismiss all" and each row with "Dismiss" (app.acknowledge_alert) and a jump such as "Count stock", "Open expiry" or "See what is low".
Roles: manager, owner.
Not a rail row: reached from inside another screen or by URL.

chunks.title: /stock/counts
chunks.body:
"Stock count": "Start count" opens a count (app.start_count), a blind-entry table follows (drafts saved locally, with a "Show recorded amounts" toggle), and "Finish count" confirms and calls app.finalize_count, then opens Count differences.
Roles: manager, owner.
Not a rail row: reached from inside another screen or by URL.

chunks.title: /stock/expiry
chunks.body:
Expiry, from app.report_stock: an "Expired: throw out and write off" panel and an "Expiring soon: use first" panel listing batches with quantity left, worth and date; "Write off" opens a manager-PIN and reason dialog that calls app.write_off_expired, and the header has "Export".
Roles: manager, owner.
Not a rail row: reached from inside another screen or by URL.

chunks.title: /stock/ingredients
chunks.body:
Ingredient master data (unit, supplier, pack size and price, shelf life, par, reorder point, yield, expected waste) from the ingredients table; "New ingredient" and per-row "Edit" open a dialog whose "Save" writes app.upsert_ingredient, and on-hand is a read-only figure linking to "Count stock".
Roles: manager, owner.
Not a rail row: reached from inside another screen or by URL.

chunks.title: /stock/margins
chunks.body:
Margins per menu item from v_item_margin: an "Items that earn too little" panel with "Show which" for "Sell at a loss" and "Margin under 30%", over a searchable Price, Cost to make, Margin and Margin % table; read-only, and the empty state links to Recipes.
Roles: manager, owner.
Not a rail row: reached from inside another screen or by URL.

chunks.title: /stock/products
chunks.body:
"Shop products": one row per size of every Touch Shop product (a menu item in a shop section) with SKU, barcode, price, on hand and supplier; "New product" writes app.upsert_menu_item then app.upsert_retail_variant, "Add size" and "Edit" write app.upsert_retail_variant, which keeps each size's own stock row (unit pc) in step. For a manager a product's prices go to the owner: a new product is saved hidden, a hidden product never on sale keeps its prices editable and offers "Put on sale" (a shop_launch price or promo change on /protocols), and a product on sale has its prices read-only with "Change the price" in place of "Add size", while its SKU, barcode, supplier, pack cost and low-stock level stay editable.
Roles: manager, owner.
Not a rail row: reached from inside another screen or by URL.

chunks.title: /stock/receive
chunks.body:
"Goods in": "Bought by the driver" lists the driver's purchases still to receive (app.purchases_to_receive), and "Receive" opens one (?purchase=) prefilled with what was bought, where "Receive into stock" books its stock lines as one delivery through app.receive_purchase and "Mark checked" closes a line that is not stock (app.acknowledge_purchase_line); each purchase says "Delivered <time> by <name>" once the driver confirmed it reached the venue on the phone, or "Delivery not confirmed yet", and receiving never waits for it; below it, one delivery per submit with supplier and notes and per-line ingredient, received and ordered quantities, cost per unit and batch expiry; "Add another ingredient" adds a line and "Record delivery" posts the whole delivery through app.receive_delivery.
Roles: manager, owner.
Not a rail row: reached from inside another screen or by URL.

chunks.title: /stock/recipes
chunks.body:
Recipes tabbed by Menu items, Add-ons and Prepared items with an All or No-recipe filter; "Add" or "Edit" opens a dialog where "Add an ingredient" adds lines and "Save" replaces the whole recipe atomically through app.set_recipe.
Roles: manager, owner.
Not a rail row: reached from inside another screen or by URL.

chunks.title: /stock/suppliers
chunks.body:
"Suppliers": who the venue buys from (name, phone, notes, in use), picked on goods in and on shop products; "New supplier" and "Edit" write app.upsert_supplier, which refuses a second live supplier with the same spelling.
Roles: manager, owner.
Not a rail row: reached from inside another screen or by URL.

chunks.title: /stock/variance
chunks.body:
"Count differences" for a chosen finished count from v_variance_report, defaulting to "Only differences" with a toggle to "All ingredients", with columns Records said, Counted, Difference, Sold, Expected waste, Recorded waste, Voids, Expired and Product tests (what a new item's test servings used, the product_test movements of a product release); each row has "History", where a product test's note opens its release on /protocols, and the header has "Export".
Roles: manager, owner.
Not a rail row: reached from inside another screen or by URL.

chunks.title: /stock/waste
chunks.body:
"Waste & production", two forms side by side: "Record waste" (ingredient, quantity, Spill or Spoilage, a required note) writes app.record_waste, and "Record production" (prepared item, amount made) writes app.record_production, which consumes the components by recipe and reports the batch cost; below them "Made today" lists the business day's batches, from here or the kitchen's phones, with who made them (app.production_log_today).
Roles: manager, owner.
Not a rail row: reached from inside another screen or by URL.

chunks.title: /tasks — My tasks
chunks.body:
"My tasks", the driver's and marketing's landing screen and the team workspace's one rail row; nothing can be assigned yet, so it shows only the empty state saying what will appear here once assigned (purchases and checklists for a driver, marketing tasks and checklists for marketing), with no buttons and no data read.
Roles: driver, marketing.
Reached from: Team: "My tasks".

chunks.title: /till — Till
chunks.body:
The cashier's till: a search box, category strip and item grid feed a basket whose "Send to kitchen" posts the order (order.add_items → app.till_add_items), the active tab panel's "Cash" and "Card" buttons open the payment pane (tab.settle → app.settle_tab), and "New tab" (F6) opens a tab.
Roles: cashier, manager, owner.
Reached from: Till: "Till".

chunks.title: /till/drawer — Cash drawer
chunks.body:
The "Cash drawer" screen showing the opening float and today's drawer activity; "Open drawer" asks for a reason code and records the opening with app.record_drawer_open, and managers also see "Go to day close".
Roles: cashier, manager, owner.
Reached from: Till: "Cash drawer"; Management › Financial: "Cash drawer".

chunks.title: /till/tabs — Open tabs / Tills
chunks.body:
The "Open tabs" board listing every tab on the floor with its age and running total; "Open tab" starts a new one, a row's "Open" jumps to the till with that tab selected, "Merge" combines two tabs (app.merge_tabs), and "Remove" cancels an empty tab (app.cancel_tab).
Roles: cashier, manager, owner.
Reached from: Till: "Open tabs"; Operations: "Open tabs"; Management › Observe: "Tills" (not a printed rail row).

chunks.title: /workspaces
chunks.body:
The "Choose a workspace" switcher, shown when an account holds more than one role; each workspace tile is a button that makes that workspace active and opens its home, with a "You are here" badge on the current one.
Roles: manager, owner.
Not a rail row: reached from inside another screen or by URL.

chunks.title: tool analytics_best_sellers
chunks.body:
The top-selling menu items in a range by units and revenue.
Kind: aggregate. Scope: cafe. Loaded on demand.
Same numbers on the page: /analytics/cafe.
Database function: app.analytics_best_sellers (through app.assistant_run_tool).
Arguments:
  from (date, required) — First business day of the range, YYYY-MM-DD.
  to (date, required) — Last business day of the range, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive).
  limit (integer 1..100) — How many items (default 10).
  basis (enum: settled | served) — Sales basis: 'settled' (paid tabs, the default the pages use) or 'served'.
Result: the result is itself the row array; id columns item_id get handles.

The audit log: who did what, when, to which record, with the reason code and the changed fields. Filter by time, actor, action prefix (e.g. "tab.", "reservation.") and free text. Answers "who changed X".
Kind: list. Scope: audit. Always loaded.
Same numbers on the page: /admin/audit.
Database function: app.assistant_audit_page (through app.assistant_run_tool).
Arguments:
  from (timestamp) — Earliest event time, ISO 8601.
  to (timestamp) — Latest event time, ISO 8601 (exclusive).
  actor (id) — Only this staff member (id or handle).
  action_prefix (string) — Only actions starting with this (e.g. "tab.discount").
  text (string) — Free text matched against action, entity, reason and the changed keys.
  limit (integer 1..500) — Rows to return, 1–500. Default 50.
  offset (integer 0..) — Rows to skip, for paging.
Result: rows under "rows"; id columns id, actorId, authorizerId, entityId get handles.
List tool: paged, at most 500 rows per call, countable for the job estimator (200 rows per job chunk).

chunks.title: tool propose_job
chunks.body:
Propose a job instead of reading many rows in the chat. Call this when a request needs more than one page (500 rows) of any list tool, or says "all", "every" or names a large number. Nothing runs; the owner sees an estimate with the exact row count and the price and decides.
Kind: meta. Scope: howto. Always loaded.
No page shows this directly.
Served by the assistant-chat edge function itself.
Arguments:
  question (string, required) — The question the job answers, in the owner's words.
  steps (object, required) — The list tool calls the job would make, as {"calls":[{"tool":"payments_list","args":{...}}]}, without limit/offset — the job pages them itself. Also "extract": one sentence on what each chunk should extract, and "reduce": how the chunks combine.
  aggregate_alternative (object) — Optional: aggregate tool calls that could answer most of the question now, as {"calls":[...]} — shown to the owner as the recommended cheaper way.
Result: an object of aggregates (key/value lines).

chunks.title: app.accept_terms
chunks.body:
Records that the calling account accepted Terms/Privacy version p_version, stamped with the server clock. Refuses an anonymous café session and a deleted account (ACCOUNT_REQUIRED) and a malformed version (VERSION_INVALID). The only write path to profiles.terms_version / terms_accepted_at.
Signature: app.accept_terms(p_version text default null) returns jsonb.
Granted to: authenticated. Guard: not detected by pattern — read the migration.
Writes no audit row of its own (or via a helper).
Error codes: AUTH_REQUIRED, ACCOUNT_REQUIRED, VERSION_INVALID.
Not called directly by the operator app (edge function, guest app, queue or internal).
Defined in migration 0153 (last definition). The assistant cannot call this; it only explains it.

Error codes: FORBIDDEN, PROTOCOL_NOT_FOUND, SUBMISSION_DECIDED, PROTOCOL_CLOSED.

chunks.title: table assistant_chunks
chunks.body:
0110. One searchable piece of text the assistant may cite: a system-map entry (page, nav, rpc, action, table, column, setting, enum, label, rule, doc, system) or a free-text row (note, request, alert, finding, rejection, menu_item, promotion). Written by the assistant-index edge function under the service role; read through app.assistant_search.
Created in migration 0110.
Columns:
  id bigint generated always as identity primary key
  kind text not null check (kind in ( 'page','nav','rpc','action','table','column','setting','enum','label','rule','doc','system', 'note','request','alert','finding','rejection','menu_item','promotion')) — What the chunk describes; the scope checkboxes map to kinds (catalog SCOPE_CHUNK_KINDS).
  ref text not null — Stable identity of the source: a route, a function name, table.column, or a row id.
  lang text not null check (lang in ('en', 'ar')) — en or ar. Map entries exist in both where an Arabic label exists.
  title text
  body text not null — The cleaned text (phones and emails already pseudonymised by the cleaning function).
  route text — Where the thing lives in the operator app, so an answer can link to it.
  embedding extensions.vector(1024) — 1024-dim embedding from the configured provider (voyage / openai / local zero-padded); null when the provider is none.
  tsv tsvector generated always as (to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(title, '') || ' ' || body)) stored — Generated: simple-config tsvector over title and body.
  source_updated_at timestamptz — When the source row or file last changed, so an answer can say how old a text hit is.
  indexed_at timestamptz not null default now() — When this chunk was last (re)written.

chunks.title: table assistant_component_cache
chunks.body:
0141. One generated answer of a component for one parameter set and one state of its inputs (plan §2.8). Served by app.analytics_component while superseded_at is null and expires_at has not passed. Written only by the assistant-component edge function through app.assistant_component_upsert.
Created in migration 0141.
Columns:
  id bigint generated always as identity primary key
  component_key text not null references assistant_components(key) on delete cascade
  params_hash text not null — md5 of the canonical parameters (app.assistant_params_hash): range, compare basis, scope, court, language.
  inputs_fingerprint text not null — sha256 of the cleaned tool results the answer read. Same numbers, same fingerprint, no new generation.
  content jsonb not null — The model's answer, shaped by the component's output_schema.
  sources jsonb not null default '[]'::jsonb — [{name, args, row_count, ms, route, stats}] — every tool call behind the answer.
  gate jsonb — The number gate's verdict on the answer (plan §4.5).
  tokens jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb — {"model", "input", "cache_write", "cache_read", "output", "cost_micros"} — what this generation cost; the card prints it.
  generated_at timestamptz not null default now() — When the model wrote it; the card always prints this line.
  expires_at timestamptz — Optional hard expiry; null means "until superseded".
  superseded_at timestamptz — Set when a newer generation landed for the same parameters or the edge function saw the numbers move. The card shows a superseded row greyed as "the last answer".

chunks.title: table assistant_components
chunks.body:
0141. An analytics card the assistant pipeline fills (plan §5.4): a fixed question, the catalog tools that answer it and the JSON schema the model must return. builtin rows are seeded by migration; pinned rows come from app.assistant_pin_component. Archived rows stay for their cache history.
Created in migration 0141.
Columns:
  key text primary key check (key ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,63}$') — Stable id used by the page and the cache: cafe_findings, courts_findings, week_paragraph, what_changed, stock_watch, staff_note, or a pinned key.
  kind text not null check (kind in ('builtin', 'pinned')) — builtin (seeded) or pinned (owner pressed "Pin to Analytics" on a chat answer).
  question text not null check (length(question) between 1 and 4000) — The single user turn the model answers, in English; the answer is written in the page language.
  output_schema jsonb not null — JSON schema for output_config.format (strict: every property required, additionalProperties false). The card renders content against it.
  tools text[] not null check (cardinality(tools) between 1 and 12) — Catalog tool names (packages/core/src/assistant/tools.ts), each optionally followed by one space and a JSON object of fixed arguments, e.g. stock_view {"view":"expiring_soon","limit":50}. Range, compare, court and language come from the card's parameters.
  default_params jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb — Parameters merged UNDER the request's: {"scope": "cafe", "compare": "previousPeriod"}. The page's own range always wins.
  created_by uuid references staff(id) — The owner who pinned it; null for built-ins.
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
  archived_at timestamptz — Set by app.assistant_archive_component; the page hides archived cards.

chunks.title: table assistant_conversations
chunks.body:
0108. One owner chat with the assistant. scopes = the context checkboxes (plan §5.5); range = the date range the checkboxes read; handles = the short-id table (r1, c2, …) the edge function owns; tokens = rolled-up counts. Archived rows keep their messages.
Created in migration 0108.
Columns:
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid()
  owner_id uuid not null references staff(id) — The owner account that opened the chat (staff.id = auth.uid()).
  title text — First 60 characters of the first question; the UI shows it in the list.
  scopes text[] not null default '{howto}' — Context scopes this chat may read: cafe, courts, money, stock, staff, customers, audit, marketing, settings, system, howto, docs, tables. Validated by app.assistant_set_scopes.
  range jsonb — Optional {"from": "YYYY-MM-DD", "to": "YYYY-MM-DD"} the context packs and default tool ranges use.
  handles jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb — Handle table {"r1": "<uuid>", "c2": "<uuid>", …, "_next": {"r": 2, "c": 3}} — the edge function owns the format; the database stores it.
  tokens jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb — Rolled-up token counts for the chat: {"input", "cache_write", "cache_read", "output", "cost_micros"}.
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
  archived_at timestamptz — Set by app.assistant_archive_conversation; the UI hides archived chats. Never deleted.
  model text — 0140. This chat's model, or NULL to follow venue_settings.llm_default_model. Must be a key of llm_pricing. Set by app.assistant_set_model; the edge function resolves the effective model per answer and stamps it on every assistant_calls row.

chunks.title: table assistant_index_queue
chunks.body:
0110. Outbox for the text index: one row per source change (kind, ref, op). Filled by the after-triggers below, leased by app.claim_due_index (60 s), deleted by app.assistant_index_done; failures keep the row with last_error for up to 5 attempts; tp_assistant_index_prune removes claimed leftovers after 7 days.
Created in migration 0110.
Columns:
  id bigint generated always as identity primary key
  kind text not null
  ref text not null
  op text not null check (op in ('upsert', 'delete')) — upsert (re-read the source and rewrite the chunk) or delete (the source row is gone).
  enqueued_at timestamptz not null default now()
  claimed_at timestamptz — Lease stamp: a row claimed within the last 60 s is skipped by the next claim and by the nudge.
  attempts int not null default 0 — Claims so far; rows stop being offered at 5.
  last_error text

chunks.title: table assistant_jobs
chunks.body:
0108. A proposed read over more rows than a chat turn may hold (plan §6). estimate holds the numbers the owner accepted; the state machine lives in app.assistant_job_transition (0112). Written by the assistant-job edge function under the service role; the owner reads it and may cancel.
Created in migration 0108.
Columns:
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid()
  conversation_id uuid references assistant_conversations(id) on delete cascade
  message_id uuid references assistant_messages(id) on delete set null
  status text not null default 'estimated' check (status in ('estimated','accepted','running','reducing','done','failed','cancelled','over_estimate')) — estimated → accepted → running → {reducing → done | over_estimate → running | failed | cancelled}; estimated/accepted → cancelled.
  plan jsonb not null — The JobPlan the model proposed: question, list-tool calls without paging, extract and reduce instructions.
  estimate jsonb not null — The JobEstimate shown to the owner: rows, chunks, tokens by kind, the price at the time, assumptions.
  mode text check (mode in ('live', 'batch')) — live (runs inside the function call) or batch (submitted to the provider's batch API and polled by cron).
  chunks_total int — How many row chunks the plan pages through.
  chunks_done int not null default 0 — Chunks finished so far; the UI polls this at 2 s.
  tokens jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb — Actual spend so far, four kinds plus cost_micros; over_estimate when it passes estimate × 1.25.
  result jsonb — The reduced answer object once done.
  error text — Why it failed, when it did.
  batch_id text — Provider batch id for mode = batch.
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
  started_at timestamptz
  finished_at timestamptz

chunks.title: table assistant_messages
chunks.body:
0108. One turn of a chat. content holds the provider's content blocks verbatim (text, tool_use, tool_result, thinking) because the next turn must replay them unchanged; sources is the UI list of tool calls and cited chunks; gate is what the answer gate found (plan §4.5).
Created in migration 0108.
Columns:
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid()
  conversation_id uuid not null references assistant_conversations(id) on delete cascade
  seq int not null — Position in the conversation, 1-based, unique per conversation.
  role text not null check (role in ('user', 'assistant')) — user or assistant.
  content jsonb not null — Provider content blocks, verbatim. Never rewritten.
  sources jsonb not null default '[]'::jsonb — [{call_id, name, args, row_count, ms, route, stats, error?}] — every tool call behind this answer, so the owner can open the page with the same figure.
  gate jsonb — {status: ok|unverified, unverified: [{raw, value}], checked, retried} — the number gate's verdict on this answer.
  tokens jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb — Token counts for this message: {"input", "cache_write", "cache_read", "output", "cost_micros"}.
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()

chunks.title: table venue_settings
chunks.body:
Created in migration 0006.
Columns:
  id boolean primary key default true check (id)
  venue_name text not null
  currency char(3) not null default 'IQD'
  timezone text not null default 'Asia/Baghdad'
  opening_hours jsonb not null — {"mon":[["09:00","23:00"]],...} config blob
  closed_dates date[] not null default '{}'
  hold_ttl_seconds int not null default 300
  protected_horizon_hours int not null default 48 — degraded-mode lockout window
  heartbeat_stale_seconds int not null default 45 — till POSTs every 10s; stale past this
  table_token_ttl_minutes int not null default 90 — guest session inactivity expiry
  waiter_call_cooldown_seconds int not null default 120
  cancellation_window_hours int not null default 12
  cash_rounding_iqd int not null default 1 — 1 = no rounding (override #1)
  expiring_soon_days int not null default 3
  tax_inclusive boolean not null default false
  phone text
  max_live_holds_per_guest int not null default 3 — 0048/C1: cap on unexpired pending holds per auth.uid(). 0 disables the cap.
  max_booking_horizon_days int not null default 180 — 0048/C1: how far ahead a guest may hold a slot. 0 disables the horizon. Default 180 is deliberately generous -- it exists to bound the C1 abuse (holds arbitrarily far out, forever), not to shorten the venue booking window; max_live_holds_per_guest is the tight constraint. Tighten here if Touch wants a shorter window.
  llm_daily_request_limit int not null default 200 — 0079/SEC-29. Insight REQUESTS per calendar day (one request fans out to ~6 model calls). The control that bites without needing a price to be right. 0 disables the LLM path entirely.
  llm_monthly_cost_cap_micros bigint not null default 20000000 — 0079/SEC-29. Hard month-to-date ceiling in USD micros (20000000 = USD 20). Enforced against llm_cost_micros_per_mtok, which is an ESTIMATE until somebody sets it from Groq's real price list.
  llm_cost_micros_per_mtok bigint not null default 500000 — 0079/SEC-29. USD micros per 1,000,000 tokens, prompt and completion blended. A SETTING, not a constant: nobody in this repo can verify Groq's price list, so the default is a conservative stand-in.
  guest_orders_per_minute int not null default 6 — 0082/SEC-25. Orders one guest table session may submit per rolling minute. 6 is generous for a real table — a group ordering in waves — and far below what a script does. 0 disables guest ordering entirely.
  guest_items_per_order int not null default 40 — 0082/SEC-25. Line items in a single guest order. 40 covers a large table; it stops one request queueing hundreds of tickets.
  tab_confirm_threshold_iqd bigint not null default 150000 — 0082/SEC-25. Tab value above which the TILL asks staff to confirm before adding more. Advisory: read by the operator UI, not enforced here — a genuine large tab must never be blocked by the database mid-service.
  llm_pricing jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb — 0111. Price per model in USD micros per 1,000,000 tokens, four kinds: {"claude-opus-5": {"input": 5000000, "cache_write": 6250000, "cache_read": 500000, "output": 25000000}}. A model absent here is priced at llm_cost_micros_per_mtok for every kind. Must change when the model changes.
  venue_id uuid — 0139 (0126): the venue this singleton describes. Defaults to app.current_venue_or_default() (granted to every writing role) — 0126 used app.default_venue(), which only service_role may execute, so a client insert would have failed at the default. ONE ROW through slice 1.
  llm_default_model text not null default 'claude-opus-5' — 0140/0142. The chat model a new assistant conversation uses unless it names one. Must be a key of llm_pricing. The vendor follows the id: claude-* is Anthropic (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), anything else is Groq (GROQ_API_KEY). Set by app.assistant_set_default_model or the usage page.

chunks.title: view v_item_cogs
chunks.body:
View, defined in migration 0019.
Definition: with (security_invoker = on) as select v.id as variant_id, v.item_id, mi.name_en as item_name_en, mi.name_ar as item_name_ar, v.name_en as variant_name_en, v.name_ar as variant_name_ar, v.price_iqd, sum(rl.qty / (i.yield_percent / 100.0) * c.unit_cost_iqd) as cogs_iqd from menu_item_variants v join menu_items mi on mi.id = v.item_id join recipe_lines rl on rl.variant_id = v.id join ingredients i on i.id = rl.ingredient_id left join lateral ( select coalesce( (select b.unit_cost_iqd from stock_batches b where b.ingredient_id = i.id order by b.received_at desc, b.id desc limit 1), i.pack_cost_iqd / nullif(i.pack_size, 0), 0) as unit_cost_iqd ) c on true group by v.id, v.item_id, mi.name_en, mi.name_ar, v.name_en, v.name_ar, v.price_iqd

chunks.title: view v_variance_report
chunks.body:
View, defined in migration 0172.
Definition: with (security_invoker = on) as with counts as ( select c.id, c.finalized_at, c.counted_by, lag(c.finalized_at) over (order by c.finalized_at) as period_start from stock_counts c where c.finalized_at is not null ) select c.id as count_id, c.period_start, c.finalized_at as period_end, l.ingredient_id, i.name_en, i.name_ar, i.unit, l.theoretical_qty, l.counted_qty, l.counted_qty - l.theoretical_qty as variance_qty, p.sold_qty, round(p.sold_qty * i.waste_allowance_percent / 100.0, 3) as expected_waste_qty, p.recorded_waste_qty, p.void_qty, p.expired_qty, p.movement_ids, p.product_test_qty from stock_count_lines l join counts c on c.id = l.count_id join ingredients i on i.id = l.ingredient_id left join lateral ( select coalesce(-sum(sm.qty_delta) filter (where sm.movement_type = 'sale_consumption'), 0) as sold_qty, coalesce(-sum(sm.qty_delta) filter (where sm.movement_type in ('waste_spill','waste_spoilage')), 0) as recorded_waste_qty, coalesce(-sum(sm.qty_delta) filter (where sm.movement_type = 'void_after_send'), 0) as void_qty, coalesce(-sum(sm.qty_delta) filter (where sm.movement_type = 'expired_writeoff'), 0) as expired_qty, array_agg(sm.id order by sm.id) as movement_ids, coalesce(-sum(sm.qty_delta) filter (where sm.movement_type = 'product_test'), 0) as product_test_qty from stock_movements sm where sm.ingredient_id = l.ingredient_id and sm.at <= c.finalized_at and (c.period_start is null or sm.at > c.period_start) ) p on true

chunks.title: op.errors (packages/i18n/src/catalogs/en.ts)
chunks.body:
SLOT_TAKEN: That slot was just taken — pick another time.
DEGRADED_LOCKOUT: The venue is in offline mode — this action is blocked right now.
PIN_INVALID: Incorrect PIN.
PIN_LOCKED: Too many wrong PINs — locked for a few minutes.
PIN_OWN: That is your own PIN. Another manager has to enter theirs.
PIN_GRANT_REQUIRED: Manager authorisation expired — enter the PIN again.
FORBIDDEN: You do not have permission for that.
AUTH_REQUIRED: You must be signed in.
ALREADY_NOTIFIED: Staff have already been notified for this table.
NO_OPEN_DAY: No business day is open.
PREVIOUS_DAY_OPEN: Close the previous day before opening a new one.
DAY_OPEN_TABS: Open tabs remain — settle or void them before closing the day.
DAY_UNSYNCED: A till still has queued offline writes — let it finish syncing.
INVALID_DURATIONS: Duration options must be 30–300 minutes in 15-minute steps.
INVALID_ACTIVE_WINDOW: The court's last active day cannot be before its first.
COURT_IN_USE: That court still has bookings or price rules. Deactivate it instead — it leaves the calendar and the guest app, and the reports keep its name.
NAME_REQUIRED: Both the English and Arabic names are required.
UNIT_LOCKED: The unit is locked — the ledger already holds quantities in it.
KIND_LOCKED: The kind is locked — the ledger already classifies this ingredient.
INVALID_YIELD: Usable yield must be between 0 and 100.
INVALID_WASTE_ALLOWANCE: Waste allowance must be between 0 and 100.
INVALID_PACK: Pack size must be greater than zero.
INGREDIENT_NOT_FOUND: Ingredient not found (sub-recipes attach to a prepared ingredient).
INVALID_TARGET: Recipes attach to a size, a modifier or a prepared ingredient.
RECIPE_CYCLE: That would make a sub-recipe contain itself (or nest too deep).
COUNT_IN_PROGRESS: A count is already in progress — finalize it first.
COUNT_NOT_FOUND: Count not found.
COUNT_FINALIZED: This count is already finalized.
COUNT_LINE_NOT_FOUND: That ingredient is not part of this count.
BATCH_NOT_FOUND: Batch not found.

chunks.title: ws.analytics.courts (packages/i18n/src/catalogs/ws/analytics.en.ts)
chunks.body:
tips.occupancy: Booked minutes over the minutes the venue was open, from the opening hours with closed dates removed, times the number of courts. Every court is assumed open the same hours.
tips.revenue: The booking price of live bookings. The cafe part of a bill is not included.
tips.revPerOpenHour: Court revenue for each hour the venue was open, across all courts.
tips.pricePerBookedHour: Court revenue for each hour actually booked: what an hour of court time sells for on average.
tips.cancelRate: Cancellations over everything that was booked (live plus cancelled plus no-show). Shown as a count until there are twenty bookings.
tips.noShowRate: No-shows over everything that was booked. Shown as a count until there are twenty bookings.
tips.lost: Cancellations plus no-shows over everything that was booked (live, cancelled and no-show). Shown as a count until there are twenty bookings. Each opens its own transactions.
tips.insights: A model reads this tab's numbers and the patterns beside it, and writes findings. Each run is billed; without an AI key the findings are templates from the same numbers.
tips.attachRate: Bookings with at least one tab the till linked to them. QR orders at a cafe table are not linked, so this is the till habit as much as the guests'.
tips.heatmap: Each cell is booked minutes over the minutes every court was open in that hour, keyed by the business weekday of the booking (a 01:00 booking counts with the evening before). Maintenance blocks and retired courts are not open time. A 90-minute booking splits across the hours it covers. Hatched cells were closed.
tips.byHour: Occupancy across the period for each hour of the day, every court and weekday together.
tips.byWeekday: Occupancy across the period for each weekday, every court and hour together.
tips.duration: Live bookings by length, with the revenue each length earns per booked hour.
tips.leadTime: Time between the booking being made and its start, for one-off bookings only.

chunks.body:
tips.afterLate: الإلغاءات التي تمت بإشعار أقل من سياسة المكان ({window}) وحُجز وقتها مجددًا بحجز لاحق، مقابل التي بقيت فارغة. الإيراد المحرَّر هو سعر كل إلغاء متأخر.
tips.returning: الحجز عائد عندما يكون للضيف نفسه (حساب، أو رقم الهاتف نفسه) حجز فعلي في الأشهر الستة قبل الفترة. أعداد فقط، لا أسماء.
tips.frequency: عدد الحجوزات الفعلية لكل ضيف معرّف في الفترة.
tips.regulars: ضيوف لهم ثلاثة حجوزات فعلية أو أكثر في آخر تسعين يوماً. انقطعوا تعني لا حجز في آخر أربعة أسابيع.
tips.byWeek: الضيوف المعرّفون كل أسبوع، مقسّمين إلى من ظهروا لأول مرة ومن سبق ظهورهم.
tips.patterns: مستخرجة من حجوزات هذه الصفحة بحدود عينة صريحة. لا يُعرض ما هو دون حده؛ وفترة أوسع تكشف المزيد.

chunks.title: ws.analytics.courts (packages/i18n/src/catalogs/ws/analytics.en.ts)
chunks.body:
tips.sourceByHour: How far ahead one-off bookings were made, split by whether they were made in the app or at the desk.
tips.createdHour: The hour of the day at which one-off bookings were made, not played.
tips.seriesShare: Standing bookings are series occurrences; one-offs are everything else.
tips.holdFunnel: App holds that became bookings against holds that expired or were released by the guest. Desk holds are not counted.
tips.courtTable: One row per court over the period. The open-hours denominator is venue-wide, so occupancy assumes every court is open the same hours.
tips.losses: Cancellations and no-shows as a share of everything booked in that segment: live, cancelled and no-show, on the slot's day. A segment with fewer than twenty bookings is painted muted and printed as a count in the table, never as a rate.
tips.notice: How long before the start a cancellation was made. No-shows have no notice.
tips.lossByWho: Whether the guest or the desk cancelled, from bookings cancelled after this was recorded. The counts say how many were cancelled by the day of the slot and how many during this period.
tips.afterLate: Cancellations made with less notice than the venue's policy ({window}) whose court time was booked again by a later booking, against those that stayed empty. Freed revenue is the price of every late cancellation.
tips.returning: A booking is returning when the same guest (account, or the same phone number) had a live booking in the six months before the period. Counts only, nobody is named.
tips.frequency: How many live bookings each identified guest had in the period.
tips.regulars: Guests with three or more live bookings in the last ninety days. Gone quiet means no booking in the last four weeks.
tips.byWeek: Identified guests seen each week, split into those seen for the first time and those seen before.
tips.patterns: Mined from the bookings on this page with explicit sample floors. Nothing below its floor is shown; a wider window reveals more.
